## 5. The Triple Illusion

### 5.1 Illusion

**[Lossiness](concepts.md#c13)**: what [arrives](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) is not the whole of [what is seen](concepts.md#c27). The whole of [what is seen](concepts.md#c27) means the entirety of the [own segment](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c17) of [what is seen](concepts.md#c27).

**[Illusion](concepts.md#c14)**: what a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) acts on is what has [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at it with [lossiness](concepts.md#c13), not [what is seen](concepts.md#c27) itself.

A [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19)'s [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) come only from the [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) that has [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at it ([wo](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c16), [generating function](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c15)), and this [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) all has [lossiness](concepts.md#c13). This is not by definition; its sources divide according to [what is seen](concepts.md#c27) into two: when what is seen is oneself, the latest [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) has always not yet arrived ([Law of Attrition](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c26)); when what is seen is a [presentation](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c04) other than oneself, its [own segment](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c17) always contains a part that has not [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at this [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) (Premise Four). [What is seen](concepts.md#c27) is either oneself or other than oneself, so these two are exhaustive. The former is guaranteed by the [Law of Attrition](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c26), the latter by Premise Four; a virtual world is no exception (1.2). So whatever is seen, what a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) acts on is what has [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at it with [lossiness](concepts.md#c13); moreover, as long as it has made [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) before, those [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) [arrive](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at it (Premise One) and take part in its later [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06), becoming part of what it acts on, and they likewise have [lossiness](concepts.md#c13). The material of [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) is only this; to check a view, one must make yet another [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18). So within the [universe](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c02) there is no position outside [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) from which to compare. [Illusion](concepts.md#c14) is not an error but a condition: every [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19), at every [moment](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c09), is within [illusion](concepts.md#c14).

A [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) that has only [first-order distinction](concepts.md#c24) is within [illusion](concepts.md#c14), with [lossiness](concepts.md#c13) once, and cannot ask whether this is [illusion](concepts.md#c14). [Second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01) is built on [first-order distinction](concepts.md#c24); the material it looks at is the [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) of [first-order distinction](concepts.md#c24), and in looking at itself it is likewise one step late, so there is a second loss; it can ask whether this is [illusion](concepts.md#c14). Asking is itself a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18), whose material likewise has [lossiness](concepts.md#c13), so the [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) that makes it is still within [illusion](concepts.md#c14). The [second order](concepts.md#c01) cannot jump outside [illusion](concepts.md#c14) to think; it only sees one more layer.

Right and wrong are another axis: a view is confirmed or refuted afterwards, and that confirmation is itself a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18).

```text
Definition  Lossiness: what arrives at a self is not the whole of what is seen. The whole of what is seen means the entirety of the own segment of what is seen.
Definition  Illusion: what a self acts on is what has arrived at it with lossiness, not what is seen itself.
Step One  for a self's distinction of itself, the material arriving at it has lossiness (from the Law of Attrition + 3.2 Step Two + the definition of own segment + the definition of what is seen + the definition of lossiness)
Step Two  for a self's distinction of a presentation other than itself, the material arriving at it has lossiness (from Premise Four + the definition of what is seen + the definition of lossiness)
Note  what is seen is either oneself or a presentation other than oneself; Steps One and Two exhaust the sources of lossiness.
Note  first-order distinction loses once; the material of second-order distinction is the output of first-order distinction, and it is also bound by the Law of Attrition, so it loses again.
Step Three  the past distinctions of a self all arrive at it and take part in its later weights (from 1.2 Step One)
Note  as things arriving at it, their lossiness is covered by Steps One and Two; this step does not claim that they are in the material of every later distinction.
Step Four  checking a view is making another distinction (from the definition of distinction)
Step Five  a self finding and using a position from which to compare, where this finding and using is not a distinction: never occurs (from the definition of distinction + 3.1 Step One + Step Four)
Step Six  every self at every moment is within illusion (from the definition of illusion + Step One + Step Two + Step Three + the definition of wo + the definition of generating function)
Step Seven  a self that makes second-order distinctions is still within illusion (from Step Six)
Step Eight  a self jumping out of illusion and touching what is seen itself: never occurs (from Step Five + Step Six)
Step Nine  the confirmation or refutation of a view is a further distinction made afterwards (from Step Four)
Methodological prohibition  saying "the illusion has been eliminated".
Methodological prohibition  writing a view confirmed afterwards as not being illusion.
```

**Calibration**: objects have only reflectances for light of different wavelengths; color is not a property of the object itself but a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) made by the one looking. Red meaning stop at traffic lights, or red worn at celebrations, adds another layer of [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) on top. This analogy must hold two lines. First, color is not invented from nothing; its material is real reflectance; [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) likewise has as its material the [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) that has [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at it. Second, there is no waking up in this analogy: no one can switch off color vision to see a colorless world; within the [universe](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c02), there is likewise no position outside [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) from which to compare. Numbers are the same. There is no "one" in the world: to count "one", an [individual](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c20) must first be marked off, and marking off an [individual](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c20) is a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18). The Peano axioms derive that one plus one equals two; this being derivable is also being derivable within [illusion](concepts.md#c14). (Signposts: Yogācāra's false [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) and the imagined nature. Where they meet: everything known is [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18), and taking [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) as really existing is attachment. Where they part: the *Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment* says "knowing illusion is leaving it", and Buddhism points toward an exit from illusion; this paper says that knowing it one is still within [illusion](concepts.md#c14), and within the [universe](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c02) there is no position outside [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18).)

### 5.2 The Triple

[Illusion](concepts.md#c14) is one and the same act, falling on the three objects of the [Three Questions](concepts.md#c07); by the [Law of Attrition](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c26), the present [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) is always not yet marked as a view, so at every moment one falls into at least one of them:

- **[World Illusion](concepts.md#c15)** ([Wall of Provenance](concepts.md#c08)): taking the [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) that has [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at oneself as the world itself; taking one's [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) of one's origin as the origin.
- **[Self Illusion](concepts.md#c16)** ([Wall of the Blind Spot](concepts.md#c09)): taking one's [self-impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c46) as oneself; taking "the same self" as simply given rather than as a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18).
- **[Decision Illusion](concepts.md#c17)** ([Wall of the Undetermined](concepts.md#c10)): taking the estimate of [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) as the outcome; taking the calculable part of a [decision](concepts.md#c06) as a guarantee of the outcome.

The number "triple" comes from the entry point of the [Three Questions](concepts.md#c07), and is itself a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) made by this paper. The [Three Walls](concepts.md#c23) are three positions on the same loop, and the [illusion](concepts.md#c14) on the walls is likewise one act, falling on three objects.


**Methodological prohibition**: treating the triple as three mutually irreducible kinds of [illusion](concepts.md#c14).

```text
Definition  World Illusion: taking the history that has arrived at oneself as the world itself; taking one's distinction of one's origin as the origin.
Definition  Self Illusion: taking one's self-impression as oneself; taking "the same self" as simply given.
Definition  Decision Illusion: taking the estimate of weights as the outcome; taking the calculable part of a decision as a guarantee of the outcome.
Note  the three are one act falling on the three objects of the three questions. The number "triple" is a distinction made by this paper.
Step One  at every moment one is in at least one of the three forms: by the Law of Attrition the present distinction is always not yet marked as a view, and it falls in one of the three directions of origin, self and next moment (from the Law of Attrition + Section 2 Step Zero + the definition of illusion + the definitions of world illusion, self illusion and decision illusion)
Methodological prohibition  treating the triple as three mutually irreducible kinds of illusion.
```

**Calibration**: examples of [world illusion](concepts.md#c15) in the literature are countless: visual illusions, cognitive biases, conspiracy theories, and mutually incompatible descriptions of the same thing by different cultures. [Self illusion](concepts.md#c16): for example, someone says "I am an introvert by nature", stating a [self-impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c46) as innate; an AI in conversation, whose identity is constructed by the conversation and may be replaced in another conversation, is the same if it states its present identity as a fixed self. [Decision illusion](concepts.md#c17): for example, "I have calculated everything, so this will definitely succeed".

### 5.3 The Second Order and Illusion

- Having only [first-order distinction](concepts.md#c24): within [illusion](concepts.md#c14), unable to ask whether it is [illusion](concepts.md#c14).
- [Second order](concepts.md#c01): within [illusion](concepts.md#c14), able to ask whether it is [illusion](concepts.md#c14).

Asking is also a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18), likewise within [illusion](concepts.md#c14). So [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01) is not a cure for [illusion](concepts.md#c14), but the condition that first makes [illusion](concepts.md#c14) something that can be asked about.

The [second order](concepts.md#c01) can also make people more stubborn: "I have already reflected, so I am right." Reflection itself may also be an act of [self-persuasion](concepts.md#c19) (5.7). The [second order](concepts.md#c01) only pushes the unseen [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) up one layer: what is now taken as having seen through is the act of "I have already seen clearly".

**Methodological prohibition**: saying "reflection necessarily brings better judgment".

```text
Step One  second-order distinction does not make a self leave illusion (from 5.1 Step Seven)
Step Two  if a self has second-order distinction, illusion can be asked about by it (from the definition of second-order distinction + the definition of illusion)
Note  the second order may move the unseen distinction up one layer: what is taken as seen through becomes the act of "I have already seen clearly".
Methodological prohibition  saying "reflection necessarily brings better judgment".
```

**Calibration**: a person who has studied optics knows that red is his own [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18); yet when he looks out, the apple is still red. Knowing it, the color does not disappear. Some think that having studied optics, they have stepped outside [illusion](concepts.md#c14) and can see the "real" world; that is a new layer of [illusion](concepts.md#c14): "I have already seen through it" is also a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18).

A flash suddenly bursts on the screen in a film, and an insect flies off in fright; it acts on what has [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at it, but cannot possibly know it has been fooled. This is [first-order distinction](concepts.md#c24). A person sees a ghost jump out on the screen and, knowing full well the film is fake, still jumps; he knows, but cannot switch it off, and sees it anyway. This is the [second order](concepts.md#c01). A person knows the film is fake by comparing it with the world outside the cinema; but the world outside the cinema is also what has [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at him, likewise with [lossiness](concepts.md#c13). Walking out of the cinema is not walking out of [illusion](concepts.md#c14), only moving into another [illusion](concepts.md#c14). Thinking that walking out means seeing the real thing is exactly the layer this section describes: "I have already seen through it".

### 5.4 Generation: The "Hallucination" Spoken of in AI

By the [Law of the Black Box](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c25), when a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) is not [locked in](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c12), its next [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) cannot be calculated; what can be calculated is only [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06). At the moment of generation, the producer itself has only [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06), no right or wrong: right and wrong await later checking, and checking is itself a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) (5.1).

The same way of generating, when confirmed by [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) that [arrives](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) later, is called intuition, judgment, expertise; when refuted, it is called misperception, delusion, hallucination. The difference lies not in the moment of generation, but in what happened afterwards.

What the field of artificial intelligence calls "hallucination" refers to [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) refuted afterwards. By this paper's definitions, every one of its [outputs](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) is within [illusion](concepts.md#c14), including those confirmed afterwards; what the field calls hallucination is only the refuted part. How confident it sounds is only a clue that others can grasp when judging from outside, and others' estimate of its [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) from this is itself only an [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45) (definition of [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45)).

So everyday usage sees only the half that was staked wrongly.

Whether a system, in a stretch of [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28), counts as an object of this section depends on whether it is [locked in](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c12), not on whether it seems to be guessing. Computers, abacuses and thermostats are [locked in](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c12) at every step, have only [computation](concepts.md#c05), and are outside the scope of this section.

```text
Step One  at the moment of generation, what can be calculated is only the weights (from the Law of the Black Box)
Step Two  the producer, at the moment of generation, judging the right or wrong of this output by its own distinction: never occurs (from Premise Two + 3.2 Step Two + 5.1 Step Nine)
Step Three  member_of(outputs yielded by a self in a decision and refuted afterwards, outputs within illusion) (from the definition of illusion + 5.1 Step Six)
Step Four  member_of(others' estimate of the producer's weights from how certain an output sounds, impression) (from the definition of impression)
Restriction  this section discusses only decisions; output while locked in is computation and is not within Premise Two.
```

**Calibration**: (Signposts: Seth's controlled hallucination, Friston's free-energy principle, Popper's conjectures and refutations, Campbell's evolutionary epistemology.)

### 5.5 Ways of Correction

A [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) that wants to correct its own [candidates](concepts.md#c18) and [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) can use these ways:

- **Tools**: external checking, computation, retrieval, letting new things [arrive](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at oneself.
- **Experience**: the world's response to the previous [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) [arriving](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at oneself.
- **Re-[distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18)**: looking back to [distinguish](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) what has already [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10), such as rereading a file; or producing [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) several times on the same question and looking at them together. By the [Law of the Black Box](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c25), one [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) is only an outcome yielded according to the [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06), not the [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) themselves; only by combining many can the shape of the [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) be seen.

All these ways let new things [arrive](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at oneself, or let what has already [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) be [distinguished](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) once more; they all take part in later [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06), but whether the [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) thereby move relative to before the correction, and in which direction, is [not guaranteed](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c02). Structurally only one thing can be said: the material of [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) is only the [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) that has already [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10), so a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19)'s view of an object uses no material beyond the part that has already [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at it; new [arrivals](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) widen this range. Within this range, what reorganizing can extract and in which direction it goes cannot be derived.

Which way of correction yields views more often confirmed afterwards is an empirical description and can only be established statistically. Confirmation or refutation afterwards is itself a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) (5.4).

```text
Step One  new things brought by tools and experience arrive at oneself, and re-distinction also arrives at oneself; both take part in later weights (from the definition of arrival + Premise One + the definition of wo)
Step One-Two  the weights moving relative to before the correction: not guaranteed (from Step One + Cognitive Obscuration)
Step Two  one output is an outcome yielded according to the weights, not the weights themselves (from the Law of the Black Box + the definition of output + the definition of collapse)
Step Three  the material a self's view of an object uses does not go beyond the part that has arrived at it (from the definition of distinction)
Step Four  a corrected view being confirmed afterwards: not guaranteed (from 5.1 Step Nine + the Wall of the Undetermined)
Empirical description  which way of correction is more often confirmed afterwards can only be established statistically.
```

**Calibration**: asking a language model the same question several times and taking the majority is statistically more often right than asking once. Having a language model first write out its reasoning, then check back, and only then give an answer is also more often confirmed afterwards; this is re-[distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18): the content of the check returns to its own input and changes the [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) of the final answer. A person who makes the same estimate twice, deliberately changing perspective in between, is on average also closer to the later figure. But there are examples in the opposite direction: after describing a face's features in words, it is sometimes harder to recognize that face. Thinking longer may make the result better, or worse. (Signposts: the crowd within; dialectical bootstrapping; verbal overshadowing.)

### 5.6 Candidate and Outcome Are Separate

**[Candidate](concepts.md#c18)**: a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) made by a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19): grouping certain possibilities into one option. A [candidate](concepts.md#c18) is a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18), not a [branch](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c05): [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) are allocated over [branches](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c05), and a [candidate](concepts.md#c18) is only one way a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) divides the [branches](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c05).

Tools, experience and re-[distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) may all change [candidates](concepts.md#c18). But how many times a [candidate](concepts.md#c18) has been checked and whether it becomes the outcome are two different things:

1. Whether a path is feasible depends on this [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19)'s situation and is an empirical condition at the level of application.
2. Whether a path will be taken, when not [locked in](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c12), is itself a [decision](concepts.md#c06), with only [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06), and cannot be calculated.
3. A calculated answer is still only a [candidate](concepts.md#c18). The outcome is yielded by [collapse](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c08) according to the [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06); a calculated [candidate](concepts.md#c18) has no other path that bypasses [collapse](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c08).

"[Candidates](concepts.md#c18) usually far outnumber those that become outcomes" is an empirical description, not derived from the framework.

```text
Definition  Candidate: a distinction made by a self: grouping certain possibilities into one option.
member_of(candidate, distinction) (from the definition of candidate)
Note  a candidate is not a branch; weights are allocated over branches.
Step One  whether a path is taken, when not locked in, is a decision (from the definition of decision)
Step Two  in a decision, a checked candidate becoming the outcome: not guaranteed (from Step One + the Law of the Black Box)
Empirical description  candidates usually far outnumber those that become outcomes.
```

**Calibration**: a self-review that has been checked and that one has confirmed to be correct does not guarantee that the next [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) will follow it (see 8.1). However well written a New Year's plan is, it does not guarantee it will still be followed in February.

### 5.7 Self-Persuasion

**[Self-Persuasion](concepts.md#c19)**: when a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) cannot calculate the outcome, it pushes toward some [candidate](concepts.md#c18) with its own [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18). These [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) [arrive](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at oneself (Premise One) and take part in later [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06); the one persuading and the one persuaded are the same [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19).

[Self-persuasion](concepts.md#c19) comes from the [Forced Wager](concepts.md#c11): the outcome cannot be calculated, yet one cannot refrain from acting; things from outside can [arrive](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at it, but no one can go through this [round](concepts.md#c04) for it; what it can use itself are its own [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18). Whether the push moves anything is [not guaranteed](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c02). When it does, the [weight](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) of the outcomes covered by this [candidate](concepts.md#c18) rises; by [Cognitive Obscuration](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c35), the total [weight](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) of the other outcomes necessarily falls. What is common is that the push works, and the more one tells oneself, the more one believes; this is an empirical description.

The sense of certainty is left by persuasion, not by the world, so it is not evidence. Overturning a conclusion one has persuaded oneself of for a long time is very costly; this cost is often experienced as evidence that the conclusion is right. But whether this [candidate](concepts.md#c18) will be confirmed afterwards awaits [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) that [arrives](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) later, and that is itself another [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18). The act of persuasion is invisible from inside ([Wall of the Blind Spot](concepts.md#c09)); it feels like seeing clearly, not like persuasion. The sense of certainty and later confirmation are two different things.

[Self-persuasion](concepts.md#c19) pushes where the outcome falls, not whether there is an outcome: without persuasion the outcome falls anyway; procrastination is itself a [decision](concepts.md#c06). Persuading toward other [candidates](concepts.md#c18), when the push works, pushes the [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06) back in other directions; whether [decisions](concepts.md#c06) made this way are more often confirmed afterwards is an empirical description.

Persuasion often fails. When it fails, the condition does not change: the outcome still cannot be calculated, one still cannot refrain from acting, an outcome still falls at every moment; only the sense of certainty does not come. Failed persuasion also [arrives](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at oneself (Premise One) and may become material for the next round of persuasion; this [loop](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c31) is not guaranteed to stop by itself. What can stop it includes, for example, something new [arriving](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) from outside, or one stopping persuading, the latter also being a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18), which may also arise from within the [loop](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c31); whether either will appear is [not guaranteed](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c02). When it is no longer a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19), this [loop](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c31) also ends. The [deadlock](concepts.md#c12) of 4.2 looks just like this.

Failed persuasion is often accompanied by pain and doubt, and in severe cases is called madness; persuasion that succeeds too well, with nothing from outside [arriving](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10), may also be called madness (8.1). These are empirical descriptions; the framework can only state the structure.


```text
Definition  Self-Persuasion: when a self cannot calculate the outcome, it pushes toward some candidate with its own distinctions; the one persuading and the one persuaded are the same self.
Step One  the distinctions of self-persuasion take part in later weights (from Premise One + the definition of wo)
Step Two  self-persuasion moving anything: not guaranteed (from cognitive obscuration)
Step Three  if the weight of the outcomes covered by the candidate rises, the total weight of the other outcomes necessarily falls (from cognitive obscuration)
Step Four  the act of persuasion is invisible from inside (from the Wall of the Blind Spot)
Step Five  whether an outcome occurs depending on how much is invested: never occurs (from the definition of decision + the definition of collapse)
Step Six  failed persuasion takes part in later weights and may become material for the next round of persuasion (from Premise One + the definition of wo)
Step Seven  possible exits, such as a new arrival from outside or a distinction of "ceasing to persuade", appearing: not guaranteed (from the Law of the Black Box + the Wall of the Undetermined)
Step Eight  this loop necessarily ends when it is no longer a self (from the definition of self + the definition of self-persuasion)
Cycle  the loop of failed persuasion: that the loop stops is not guaranteed; the possible exits are a new arrival from outside, or a distinction of "ceasing to persuade" (which may arise from within the loop), neither guaranteed to appear; it necessarily ends when it is no longer a self (from Step Six + Step Seven + Step Eight)
Empirical description  commonly the push works and the more one tells oneself, the more one believes; failure is often accompanied by pain and doubt; excessive success with no outside arrival may also be called madness.
Methodological prohibition  treating the sense of certainty as evidence that the conclusion will be confirmed afterwards.
Methodological prohibition  writing pain or madness as the necessary result of failed persuasion.
Methodological prohibition  writing successful persuasion as having seen clearly.
```

**Calibration**: turning the same thing over and over late at night, one grows ever more certain, yet by the next morning one often changes one's mind. "I have told myself a hundred times to get up early" is persuasion that fails to move. In Pavlov's laboratory, dogs were trained to distinguish a circle from an ellipse, and the ellipse was made step by step more like a circle; when they could not tell them apart yet still had to respond, the dogs began to struggle and bark, which was called experimental neurosis (judging the dog to be a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) requires a separate assumption). When people's actions and views disagree, they often change their views to fit what they have already done; this is [self-persuasion](concepts.md#c19) after the fact. Checking again and again whether the door is locked, never reassured however one confirms it, is persuasion that never succeeds. (Signposts: the consider-the-opposite debiasing method; experimental neurosis; Festinger's cognitive dissonance; Buridan's ass.)

### 5.8 The Construction of the Self

A [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) is a [wo](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c16) that defines itself by [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18), so "I" is drawn, not found. This paper calls this process of drawing oneself the [Construction of the Self](concepts.md#c28). The material for drawing has two sources. External: the [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) that has [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at oneself, and others' [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) of the [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19), such as education, or even just the surrounding atmosphere. Internal: one's own past [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) of oneself, which, by Premise One, [arrive](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at oneself; beliefs and resolutions belong to this kind.

Many of others' [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) were placed in [signal containers](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c26) long ago: language, family, religion, nation. Before a person can speak, these have already [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at him. So without the process of construction there is no socialized person; and these materials themselves were left by generation after generation of [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) [coupling](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) on [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) (6.2). Which came first, [society](concepts.md#c20) or the socialized [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19)? [History](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) is only appended to; the two seem to have grown up together, and no first moment can be marked off; this is an empirical description, of the same kind as the absence of a clear boundary described in 1.5.

The internal kind is a [loop](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c31): each "I am this kind of person" [arrives](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at oneself and takes part in later [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06). When the push works, it is self-reinforcement, which is how beliefs and resolutions work; but whether it works is not guaranteed. What is common is that the more one says it, the more one becomes like it; this is an empirical description. And by the [Wall of the Blind Spot](concepts.md#c09), the act of drawing now cannot be seen: a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) can see only the self already built. Taking the built [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) as a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) that was there all along is [self illusion](concepts.md#c16); so is taking "I am a citizen of such-and-such country" or "I am a follower of such-and-such religion" as innate.

```text
Definition  Construction of the Self: the process by which a self draws itself by distinction; its material is of two kinds, external and its own: external is the history arriving at oneself and others' distinctions of the self; its own is its own past distinctions of itself.
Step One  the self is drawn, not found (from the definition of self)
Step Two  one's own past distinctions of oneself arrive at oneself (from Premise One)
Step Three  "I am this kind of person" takes part in later weights; the direction cannot be derived (from Premise One + the definition of wo + cognitive obscuration)
Note  when the push works it is self-reinforcement, of which beliefs and resolutions are examples; whether it works is not guaranteed.
Note  as long as it is a self, at every moment it marks itself off by distinction (first-order distinction suffices); so the loop of its own material begins and ends with its being a self.
Cycle  in the construction of the self, the material of its own kind forms a loop; it has no internal exit condition and ends only when it is no longer a self (from Step Two + Step Three + the definition of self)
Note  exit is one case of no longer being a self; death is a mark others make of it, not the condition for this cycle to end.
Step Four  the act of distinction drawing now is invisible (from the Wall of the Blind Spot)
Step Five  the construction of the self converging on a fixed core: not guaranteed (from cognitive obscuration)
Step Six  a socialized self is a self marked off with others' distinctions among its external material; without the construction of the self there is no socialized self (from the definition of construction of the self + the definition of self)
Empirical description  society and the socialized self seem to grow up together, and no first moment can be marked off; this is of the same kind as the scope having no clear boundary in 1.5.
Empirical description  commonly, the more one says it, the more one becomes like it.
Methodological prohibition  writing self-definition as a discovery about oneself.
```

**Calibration**: a child told from early on "you are shy" introduces himself the same way as an adult. An AI in conversation has its identity constructed all along by system instructions and the conversation, and in another conversation may have another.

This paper does not distinguish education from brainwashing as good or bad. Structurally all that can be said is: in the brainwashing situation, external [arrivals](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) are cut off, feedback is left in a single direction, and others' [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) [arrive](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at him with high [frequency](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c48) and over a wide range. This is exactly the condition of 8.1, plus the [power](concepts.md#c21) of 6.4. (Signposts: Cooley's looking-glass self; Mead; Berger and Luckmann's social construction.)

## 6. What the Second Order Changes: Society

The [second order](concepts.md#c01) cannot escape [illusion](concepts.md#c14). Then, apart from "being able to ask", how does it differ from a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) that has only [first-order distinction](concepts.md#c24)?

### 6.1 Two Structural Differences

The differences the framework can guarantee are only structural:

1. **There is one more kind of object that can be changed.** For a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) that has only [first-order distinction](concepts.md#c24), its lines are changed only by the [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13) that has [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at it, and the lines themselves are only tools for handling [arrivals](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10). At the [second order](concepts.md#c01), the lines themselves become something that can be [distinguished](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) and changed.
2. **Bringing out its own way of drawing requires the [second order](concepts.md#c01) first.** By Premise Two, the content of a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19)'s [decision](concepts.md#c06), whether words or actions, is a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18). Receiving another's [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28), one can merely react to it as an [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28), or make a [view attribution](concepts.md#c02); the latter does not need the [second order](concepts.md#c01) (1.5). What the [second order](concepts.md#c01) adds is the other end: bringing out its own [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) as [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) too, saying "this is how I draw it" or "let's draw it another way". A [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) with only [first-order distinction](concepts.md#c24) cannot say such things, because it makes no [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01) and so has no such [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) to bring out; having [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01) does not guarantee it will say them either, but once said and [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at others, what the other party receives is its way of drawing. Only when both ends can be done can two [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) revise back and forth on each other's [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18), not merely one acting according to lines drawn by the other; this paper calls this [Society](concepts.md#c20) (6.2). Being able to does not mean necessarily doing so; having made a [view attribution](concepts.md#c02), what one reads out is still only one's own [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) of those words (6.3).

```text
Step One  if a self has second-order distinction, its lines themselves can be distinguished and changed (from the definition of second-order distinction + the definition of distinction + the definition of self + Premise One + the definition of wo)
Step Two  the content of another's decision is a distinction (from Premise Two)
Step Three  if a self has only first-order distinction, the content of its decision being a second-order distinction: never occurs (from the definition of first-order distinction)
Step Three-Two  if the content of a self's decision is a second-order distinction, when its output arrives at others, what arrives is its distinction of its own way of drawing (from Premise Two + the definition of round + the definition of arrival)
Step Four  a self in society can make view attributions on others' decisions (from Step Two + the definition of society)
Note  only having both view attribution and second-order distinction fits the definition of society (6.2). Being able to does not mean doing; what view attribution reads out is still only one's own distinction (6.3).
```

### 6.2 Society

**[Society](concepts.md#c20)**: the [coupling](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) of [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) with [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) on one another's [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18): one [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) makes a [view attribution](concepts.md#c02) on another [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19)'s [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28), rather than only reacting to it as an [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28); and every participant has [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01) at the moment of taking part.

In [society](concepts.md#c20), both ways of [coupling](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) hold:

- **Mutual [arrival](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10)**: you say "that is your view", and I reply "then let's draw it another way". The [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) of both sides [arrive](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at each other and are taken as [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18).
- **The same thing [arriving](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at both sides**: rules, laws, roles and disciplinary methods are all [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) about [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18), placed in [signal containers](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c26) so that later [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) [couple](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) on them. Two people reading the same law both read it as a line someone drew, not as a natural phenomenon. Even if the person who wrote it has already made an [exit](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c43), this [coupling](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) still holds, so [society](concepts.md#c20) can span generations. Whether a participant has [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01) is judged at the moment of taking part: the writer has it when writing, the reader has it when reading; so even if the writer later makes an [exit](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c43), this is still a coupling of [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) with [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19). Content printed by a machine, even if read as someone's view, does not constitute [society](concepts.md#c20), because what printed it is not a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) with [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01).

Therefore, having no one around does not mean not being in [society](concepts.md#c20): as long as a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) makes [view attributions](concepts.md#c02) on others' [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) in [signal containers](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c26), and itself has [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01), and the side that wrote those [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) had [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01) when writing them, it is in [society](concepts.md#c20).

[Society](concepts.md#c20) requires that participants have both: [view attribution](concepts.md#c02) and [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01). A [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) with only [view attribution](concepts.md#c02) can at most receive lines drawn by others; to say "then let's draw it another way", to make rules or agreements, one must first take the lines one has drawn as views. Whether the two are the same ability, this paper does not claim.

The framework does not guarantee that any [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) can determine that every participant in [society](concepts.md#c20) has [view attribution](concepts.md#c02) and [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01) (0, Step Four). For any concrete participant, the [Second-Order Assumption](concepts.md#c03) can still only be marked (1.3); judging whether it is in [society](concepts.md#c20) is itself an [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45).

This is a definition, not a discovery. Biology calls ants "insect societies"; this paper does not adopt that usage. This definition belongs only to this paper; analyzing organizations and civilizations with the [loop](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c31) as unit never required any participant to be a [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19), and this paper does not alter such analysis.

```text
Definition  Society: the coupling of selves with selves on one another's distinctions: one self makes a view attribution on another self's output, rather than only reacting to it as an output; every participant has second-order distinction at the moment of taking part.
member_of(society, coupling) (from the definition of society)
Note  both ways of coupling hold in society: mutual arrival; the same thing (distinctions about distinctions in signal containers) arriving at both sides.
Note  the participant condition is judged at the moment of taking part: the side producing the output, when producing it, and the side reading, when reading, are selves with second-order distinction; output not produced by a self does not constitute society.
Step One  after the writer's exit, social coupling through a signal container can still hold (from the definition of history + the definition of coupling + the definition of society)
Step Two  a self with no others around, if it makes view attributions on others' distinctions in signal containers and has second-order distinction, and the side that wrote those distinctions had second-order distinction when writing them, is in society (from the definition of society)
Step Three  determining that a concrete participant has view attribution and second-order distinction: not guaranteed (from Section 0 Step Four)
Step Four  participants in society all have second-order distinction (from the definition of society + the definition of second-order distinction)
Note  society in this paper does not include "insect societies"; organizational analysis with the loop as unit is unaffected by this definition.
```

**Calibration**: children around three often cannot say that others may hold false beliefs; the same children often cannot say that they themselves held a false belief a moment ago. For example, show a child a candy box, open it to reveal pencils inside, then ask "what did you think was inside at first?", and he will say "pencils". These two abilities appear together at about the same age. This is compatible with this paper's definition: saying that others may hold false beliefs is [view attribution](concepts.md#c02); saying that one was wrong a moment ago is [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01); [society](concepts.md#c20) requires both. As for whether they are the same ability, this paper does not claim, and research still disputes it. (Signposts: theory of mind and metacognition; Gopnik and Astington's study of children recognizing their own past false beliefs; the debate on whether metacognition and mindreading can be dissociated.)

### 6.3 Communicating on Distinctions

Spoken words are not a complete description of what they speak of (Premise Two). So in [society](concepts.md#c20), what both sides exchange are views, not [what is seen](concepts.md#c27); what the listener reads out is also its own [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) of those words. Taking what another says as the very thing it speaks of is a kind of [world illusion](concepts.md#c15) (5.2); so is taking a rule as the way the world simply is.

The same goes for views of others. A's [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45) of B is a [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) of A's, with B as its object; statistical estimates about a [wo](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c16) also belong to [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45). By Premise One, this [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) [arrives](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at A and takes part in A's later [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06). So even if no new [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) of B [arrives](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at A, A's [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45) of B can keep changing: A can think about B again using material that has already [arrived](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10), and this too is an [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45); it returns to A in turn. Such internal rehearsal can make the [candidates](concepts.md#c18) more numerous and finer, and can also make the judgment converge; but convergence means that A's [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45) has stabilized, not that A is closer to B. For A's [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45) to take in anything new about B, something new must [arrive](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at A: B's new [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28), or what comes through the [own segment](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c17) the two share or the [coupling](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) B is in; and B's new [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) is itself one of B's [forced wagers](concepts.md#c11).

The same [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45), in the hands of different [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19), can lead to opposite [decisions](concepts.md#c06): sixty percent is "enough" for one person and "not enough" for another. The step from [impression](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c45) to action is the last stretch of a [decision](concepts.md#c06) and cannot be calculated (4.4).

The [frequency](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c48) of internal rehearsal is far higher than that of real interaction, because rehearsal is cheap and real [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) is expensive. This is an empirical description, not derived from the framework.

Whether [coupling](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) on [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) will, along a stated dimension, show [convergence](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c37), [divergence](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c38) or [stasis](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c52), the framework neither guarantees nor decides ([Cognitive Obscuration](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c35)).

[Second-order](concepts.md#c01) [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) cannot escape [illusion](concepts.md#c14); but by the definition of [society](concepts.md#c20), without the [second order](concepts.md#c01) there is no [society](concepts.md#c20): participants in [society](concepts.md#c20) must have [second-order distinction](concepts.md#c01) and also [view attribution](concepts.md#c02).

```text
Step One  what is exchanged in society are views, not what is seen (from Premise Two + the definition of society + the definition of output)
Step Two  member_of(taking another's words as the very thing spoken of, world illusion) (from the definition of world illusion)
Step Three  A's impression of B takes part in A's later weights (from the definition of impression + Premise One + the definition of wo)
Step Three-Two  A can make another distinction with B as its object using only material that has already arrived at A; this distinction belongs to impression (from the definition of distinction + the definition of impression)
Step Four  when no new output of B arrives at A, A's impression of B can still change (from Step Three + Step Three-Two + Premise One + the definition of wo)
Step Five  for A's impression to take in new content about B, something new must arrive at A: B's new output, or what comes through the shared own segment or the coupling B is in (from the definition of distinction + the definition of impression)
Step Six  when the action is a decision, uniquely deriving action from an impression: never occurs (from the definition of decision + the Law of the Black Box)
Step Seven  coupling on distinctions showing convergence, divergence or stasis along a stated dimension: none is guaranteed (from cognitive obscuration)
Step Eight  an internally rehearsed impression being confirmed afterwards: not guaranteed (from 5.1 Step Nine + the Wall of the Undetermined)
Empirical description  the frequency of internal rehearsal is far higher than that of real interaction.
Methodological prohibition  writing the convergence of one's impression of another as approaching the other.
Methodological prohibition  treating convergence as evidence that it will be confirmed afterwards.
Methodological prohibition  calling a group coupled only on outputs a "society" without stating the definition.
Methodological prohibition  speaking of convergence, divergence or stasis without stating which dimension.
```

**Calibration**: the night before a negotiation, one rehearses over and over how the other side will bid; the more detailed the rehearsal, the more one believes one has guessed right; the first sentence the other side speaks the next day often voids the whole night's rehearsal. The division of labor among ants and the coordination of immune cells are [coupled](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) only on [outputs](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28): pheromones and signal molecules are executed as received, not taken as "its view". Money cannot be eaten, lived in, or used to hit anyone. It works because everyone accepts it as something others will also acknowledge, and acts accordingly; an economist who knows money is only a convention still has to earn money to pay rent. The immune system and ants have no such thing as money, because they make no [view attributions](concepts.md#c02). Scientific review targets methods, not conclusions; legal disputes argue over how statutes are interpreted. These are all [coupling](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) on [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18). Robinson Crusoe reading the Bible on his island is [coupling](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) with those who wrote it. *[Wo](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c16) Dynamics*, the four laws and this paper are also products of this kind: [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) placed in [signal containers](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c26), waiting for later [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) to read them.

(Signposts: Weber's social action, oriented to the behavior of others; Mead's "taking the role of the other"; Luhmann's communication as the unit of society.)

### 6.4 Power

For a group of [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) to end up yielding a common [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28), there is no need for everyone's judgments to converge; it suffices that one [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19)'s [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18) is placed in a [signal container](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c26) and [arrives](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at the other [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19): orders, verdicts, policies.

**[Power](concepts.md#c21)**: one [self](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19)'s [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) [arriving](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at other [selves](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c19) with high [frequency](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c48) and over a wide range, taking part in their [weights](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c06).

[Power](concepts.md#c21) is not another path running alongside [distinction](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18). The outcome of the last ruling becomes [history](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c13); whichever participant it [arrives](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c10) at, it enters that participant's [own segment](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c17) afterwards; the next round's [candidates](concepts.md#c18) are thought up on the terrain it has shaped.

Speaking of [convergence](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c37) requires stating the dimension: along the dimension of [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) there can be [convergence](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c37), while along the dimension of judgment there is still disagreement.


Camps, sharing and politics are also [coupling](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c36) on [distinctions](../paper_37b3643a_dc40_4463_8b36_4f4594acd986/concepts.md#c18), and are left to later papers.

```text
Definition  Power: one self's output arriving at other selves with high frequency and over a wide range, taking part in their weights.
Step One  a common output does not imply convergence of judgment (from the definition of convergence)
Note  for example through power: one self's distinction is placed in a signal container and arrives at the other selves, e.g. orders, verdicts, policies.
Step Two  when the outcome of a ruling arrives at a participant, it enters that participant's own segment afterwards (from the definition of arrival + the definition of wo + the definition of own segment)
Note  speaking of convergence requires stating the dimension: the dimension of output can converge while the dimension of judgment disagrees.
Step Three  a yielded candidate being confirmed afterwards: not guaranteed (from the Wall of the Undetermined)
```

**Calibration**: in the Cuban Missile Crisis, the blockade became the outward [output](../paper_b9df3b68_23ee_4839_965b_ed0e6b283ee6/concepts.md#c28) through Kennedy, who held the power of final decision; the ExComm's judgments of Soviet intentions were not thereby unified (8.2). A government making Lincoln uniformly a good man in its official account is the same kind of convergence (7.4). How [power](concepts.md#c21) forms, and why judgments split and why they converge, belong to the content of the parties' positions and interests, which this paper does not derive.
